summary.intent: The user asked for further DX improvements to tackle after PR #359, then said 'Let's do all', starting with the first-release metadata preflight: catching a missing Cargo description or license before publishing rather than at the registry.
summary.outcome: Implemented a new E323 preflight check for Cargo crates missing description or license, with unit and e2e tests, docs, spec criterion and changeset. Full CI passed after formatting and the work was committed, pushed and opened as a PR. The other queued items (init output, E121 message, snapshot --tag validation, Python/Poetry issues, E030 no-root-manifest) were not started in this segment.

repo: Cargo only warns locally about missing description/license; crates.io rejects at upload, so a mixed-ecosystem release can half-publish (tags may already exist) before failing. This is why a preflight is needed.

No shared Cargo.toml fixture helper exists across tests; each test file writes its own Cargo.toml, so adding required metadata meant patching many fixtures (a script plus manual edits for raw-string fixtures and crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/mod.rs).
Adding the E323 check broke about 28 existing tests whose fixture crates lacked description/license, in both callisto-cli and callisto-graph tests.

The full derivation of publish operations requires an `origin` URL; a preflight that only needs each package's directory and crates.io targeting should read from the workspace package instead to avoid that dependency.
Cargo metadata helpers are re-exported from crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs for use by callisto-graph.
New error codes require updates to crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs, docs/errors.md (row and count), docs/publishing.md, and a criterion in docs/specs/release.json.
Repo CI (`just ci`) includes a fmt-check; formatting needed to be applied and CI rerun.

code.finding: Hosts the first-release preflight checks; the new E323 Cargo metadata check was added here and rewritten to read from the workspace package (ManifestFormat, PublishTarget) instead of full operation derivation.
Cargo adapter now contains a pure metadata check function (description/license) with unit tests in cargo/tests.rs.
Error code enum where E323 was added, next to the E322 taken-name check it mirrors.

workflow: Verify external tool behavior empirically (a probe script with real cargo) before designing a check around it.
Heredocs are refused in this environment, so use the Edit/Write tools to append to files.
Run the full test suite without stopping on first failure to measure the blast radius of a new validation before fixing fixtures.
Use a small script for bulk fixture edits, then hand-fix the outliers.
Model a new e2e test on an existing release failure test and fixture (on_branch).

friction: Heredocs were refused in the shell, forcing the Edit tool for appending tests.
The first implementation called full derivation, which needed an origin URL and failed a color-output CLI test, requiring a rewrite.
Roughly 28 existing tests broke from the new check, requiring bulk fixture patching across several test files.
Imports had to be fixed after the rewrite (PreparedOperation and RegistryKey unused; PublishTarget and ManifestFormat needed).
The first CI run failed on formatting and had to be rerun.
open_items: init output: the generated callisto.toml is just `# callisto configuration`; the output should say no config is needed. The next-steps text was not confirmed because output was cut off.
E121 message for an uncommitted first run should say to commit the files `init` wrote first.
Snapshot `--tag` validation: bad tags should fail up front with a fix.
Python `~=` precision and Poetry comment loss; deferred until users report them.
No-root-manifest repos fail with E030 at `init`; whether `init` should write a minimal callisto.toml as the root marker needs the user's design decision.
Release PR #349 should refresh itself after the merges, but this was not confirmed.
Branch name `fix/release-pr-stage-only` for PR #359 does not match its content (the `git add -A` item was dropped).
